clue.text: Road design is thrown into confusion

definitions.text: Road design is thrown into confusion

indicators.note: letters thrown into confusion are jumbled, so the three words before this phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traffic scheme has been so badly planned that the whole road layout is chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown into confusion' signals rearranging ROADDESIGNIS, and the whole clue also describes the result, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown into confusion has lost all order and system, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Sudden collapse of young lady presented with money in a church

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young lady entering society

indicators.note: the money is set in the following letters, inside them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
L is the abbreviation for pound (librae), money

explanation.surface: A debutante with cash in a church suddenly falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: The L (pound) goes in A + CE to give ACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or rout.

clue.text: Prominent foreigner in a way

indicators.note: the foreigner is placed in the way, its letters going inside

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An immigrant stands out in some respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is one that stands out, noticeable and conspicuous.

clue.text: Perhaps a bit of relaxation outside school

indicators.note: the relaxation word goes outside, around the school word

parts.note: rest means relaxation
to school is to train

explanation.surface: Some leisure outside the classroom is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of relaxation' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'Perhaps a bit', a horse's bit being an example of a restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's bit is a mouthpiece used to control it, an example of a check on movement.

clue.text: Missile used in battle — or war, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters, so or and war are rearranged

explanation.surface: A projectile used in combat, or war in general, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots an arrow, a pointed projectile, in battle.

clue.text: Fuel which is fashionable to burn

parts.note: in means fashionable
to flame is to burn

explanation.surface: Fuel that is trendy to set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel' looks like a noun but is the verb, to stoke up feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuel anger or passion is to stoke it up, to make it hotter.

clue.text: Brings out legal point supporting judge's conclusion

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below, after the judge's letter
conclusion means the end, the final letter of the judge word

parts.note: licit means legal
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A lawyer's argument backs up the judge's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legal point' looks like one phrase but is two pieces, legal and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response or information is to draw it out.

clue.text: Clear declaration under George IV for self-denial

indicators.note: in a down clue under means after
IV is the Roman numeral four, so the fourth letter of George is taken

parts.note: enunciation is clear articulation or declaration

explanation.surface: A clear statement made during George IV's reign promises self-sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George IV' looks like the king; the IV is a numeral picking the fourth letter of George.
explanation.definitionFit: Renunciation is the giving up of something, an act of abstinence or sacrifice.

clue.text: Preserves a healing influence in German city

indicators.note: the healing influence is placed in the German city, one word set within the other

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
balm is a soothing, healing thing

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy is kept in stock in a German spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve a corpse with spices and chemicals is to treat it so it does not decay.

clue.text: Disreputable service pilot, for example

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
a pilot fish is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: An air force pilot is said to be a shady character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like an airman alongside the RAF, but it is the pilot fish, an example of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffish person is rakish and of dubious reputation, flashy in an unrespectable way.

clue.text: Drunk, and giving the impression of being bombastic

parts.note: high means drunk
sounding means seeming, giving the impression of being

explanation.surface: An inebriate seems to be pompous and loud.
explanation.definitionFit: High-sounding language is pompous, grand and pretentious.

clue.text: A Continental patent can be ambiguous

parts.note: un is French for 'a', French being a Continental language
patent means obvious, plain, clear

explanation.surface: A European patent application may turn out vague in its wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' suggests a legal document, but it is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ambiguous can be read more than one way, so its meaning is not plain.

clue.text: Going about dressed in .

explanation.surface: Someone moves around wearing some garment that the next clue names.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 13 across through its dots. To wear a sailing ship is to turn it by bringing the stern through the wind, so a ship wearing is going about.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about is a sailing term for changing course, which is what a ship does when it wears; dressed in describes having clothes on the body.

clue.text: — coal, originally abandoned when split

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word coal, its opening letter only

parts.note: left means abandoned, deserted

explanation.surface: Continuing 12: someone goes around dressed in coal, which is dropped when it breaks apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is a past participle of cleave, so cleft means divided or cut in two.

clue.text: Advances in alternative form of weapons

parts.note: taken as written
crease is a variant spelling of kris (also creese), a Malay dagger, so these weapons in another spelling are creases

explanation.surface: Progress is made by switching to a different type of armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative form' is not an anagram signal: the kris, a Malay dagger, has the variant spellings creese and crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances as a noun means rises or gains, as in price advances.

clue.text: Hurry up — move forward!

explanation.surface: A pair of commands to someone who is lagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Come along is an urging to hurry; it also means to advance, to progress.

clue.text: Kind of garden centre in Carmarthen, supported by the corporation

indicators.note: the centre of the ten-letter Welsh town name is its two middle letters

parts.note: bore, past tense of bear, means carried or supported
corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A Welsh garden centre is funded by the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like the town council, but it is old slang for a large belly. 'Garden centre' seems one phrase, but 'garden' ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden devoted to growing trees.

clue.text: Country-born countess in Illyria

parts.note: Olivia is the countess in Twelfth Night, set in Illyria

explanation.surface: A countess from Shakespeare's Illyria was rustic-born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country-born' looks like one compound word; the hyphen hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American country.

clue.text: Deep regret felt about Rome's disintegration

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: disintegration breaks the word Rome's apart and reforms it

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about the fall of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is guilt and sorrow for a wrong done.

clue.text: Holy man recovered from sad humiliation

indicators.note: letters recovered from the phrase are retrieved from within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A holy man has got over a sad humiliating experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic or wandering holy man in India.

clue.text: Abnormal traumas for a tropical island

indicators.note: abnormal signals the letters are not in their normal order

explanation.surface: Unusual shocks for a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island on the equator.

clue.text: Trail horse, kept by rising composer, died

annotationWithheld.why: Trail horse, kept by rising composer, died (7): the only parse, D + GG inside ELGAR reversed (RAGLE), gives DRAGGGLE, one G too many for DRAGGLE; no reading found that accounts for the letters exactly
annotationWithheld.clue: Trail horse, kept by rising composer, died

clue.text: I attack elements of a religion

parts.note: to slam is to attack fiercely, criticise
I (iodine) and C (carbon) are chemical elements

explanation.surface: Someone declares war on the basic tenets of a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' looks like parts of a religion, but it is two chemical element symbols, I for iodine and C for carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the adjective for the faith of Muslims, so it means belonging to that religion.

clue.text: A certainty for many on edge

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, many
to edge is to inch, move slowly

explanation.surface: A sure thing for many people who are nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like nervous, but 'edge' is the verb, to move forward slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is something sure or easy.

clue.text: Group member is first to show a sign of mourning

indicators.note: the member is first, so its letters go before those of the group

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a band is a group of musicians or people

explanation.surface: One person in a group is the first to show grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a person in the group, but it is a body member, a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A black band worn round the sleeve traditionally shows that the wearer is in mourning.

clue.text: A French dish — new variant — not quite cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored, so they are rearranged
not quite means the word variant loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A new version of a French recipe comes out underdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts VARIANT to VARIAN, and 'cooked' rearranges those letters into AVARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarin is a French stew of lamb or mutton with vegetables.

clue.text: Senior officer has to accompany this figure

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
to tag on is to go along with someone, accompany them

explanation.surface: A senior army officer is obliged to escort a certain person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a person, but it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a geometric shape with eight sides.

clue.text: Fashion — the sort to succeed

parts.note: to fashion is to make or shape
taken as written
a grade is a class or sort

explanation.surface: Style is the kind of thing that wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the grade is an idiom for reaching the required standard.
